ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: After ignoring the curved arrows in the figure, an adjacent disubstituted ethane skeleton can be read; the two adjacent carbons are both chiral centers, and each is connected to one phenyl group and one hydrogen. The left chiral carbon is also connected to an oxygen atom, which is connected to a sulfonyl group S(=O)(=O), and then connected to negatively charged nitrogen, and the nitrogen is further connected to a carbonyl methoxy fragment C(=O)OC. The right chiral carbon is connected to phenyl, hydrogen, the left carbon, and the substitution site represented by a wildcard in the problem. Reasoning: The two phenyl groups are written as c1ccccc1; the heteroatom substituent is written as OS(=O)(=O)[N-]C(=O)OC. According to the specified traversal, starting from the wildcard *, passing through the two adjacent chiral carbons, and based on the wedge/dashed stereochemical information, they are written as [C@H] and [C@@H], respectively, giving the SMILES: *[C@H](c1ccccc1)[C@@H](OS(=O)(=O)[N-]C(=O)OC)c1ccccc1.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First describe the molecule in the image without using the arrows: a vicinal diphenyl ethane fragment with two stereocenters, the right stereocenter attached to *, phenyl, H, and the left carbon, and the left stereocenter attached to phenyl, H, and an O-sulfonyl-N-carboxymethyl anion group. Convert the two phenyl groups to c1ccccc1 and the heteroatom substituent to OS(=O)(=O)[N-]C(=O)OC. Choose a SMILES traversal starting at the wildcard substituent, pass through the two adjacent stereocenters, and apply the wedge/dash-derived configurations as [C@H] then [C@@H], yielding *[C@H](c1ccccc1)[C@@H](OS(=O)(=O)[N-]C(=O)OC)c1ccccc1.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中忽略弯箭头后，可读出一个相邻二取代乙烷骨架；两个相邻碳均为手性中心，并且各自连有一个苯基和一个氢。左侧手性碳还连到一个氧原子，该氧连接到磺酰基 S(=O)(=O)，再连接到带负电的氮，氮再连到羰基甲氧基片段 C(=O)OC。右侧手性碳连有苯基、氢、左侧碳以及题目中用通配符表示的取代位点。推理：两个苯基写作 c1ccccc1；杂原子取代基写作 OS(=O)(=O)[N-]C(=O)OC。按指定遍历从通配符 * 出发，经过两个相邻手性碳，并依据楔/虚线立体信息分别写为 [C@H] 和 [C@@H]，得到 SMILES：*[C@H](c1ccccc1)[C@@H](OS(=O)(=O)[N-]C(=O)OC)c1ccccc1。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the straightforward structure-to-SMILES route: identify the full connectivity and stereochemistry directly from the drawing, then encode it in canonical-style SMILES. With only one image and no answer options, this is the only genuinely distinct executable method.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the drawn transition-state skeleton while ignoring all curved arrows. Identify two adjacent stereocenters: one bearing wildcard/deuterium substituent, phenyl, H, and the neighboring carbon; the other bearing phenyl, H, the neighboring carbon, and an O-sulfamoyl carbamate substituent. Read the substituent as O-S(=O)(=O)-[N-]-C(=O)-OCH3, and read wedge/dash bonds to assign opposite configurations to the two chiral carbons.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that the required output is the SMILES expression for the transition-state structure and that curved arrows in the image should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use organic structure-to-SMILES conventions: phenyl is c1ccccc1; sulfonyl carbamate is OS(=O)(=O)[N-]C(=O)OC; implicit hydrogens on chiral carbons can be encoded by [C@H]/[C@@H]; wedge/dash stereochemistry determines @ versus @@ after choosing the written neighbor order; a wildcard attachment/deuterium-like atom in the target answer is represented by *.
